summary: CumulusMart — intermittent streaming fragment interleaving due to routing oscillation (post-incident escalation)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer CumulusMart reported intermittent streaming responses that showed interleaved fragments and partial duplicate transcripts for multi-part chat completions. Symptoms began 2026-03-10 01:20 UTC and recurred on subsequent traffic spikes. Impact: several customer-facing sessions returned mixed transcripts (segments from two separate handler instances), resulting in corrupted messages and increased token billing for duplicate partial outputs.

Impact:
- Affected ~12% of CumulusMart's streamed completions during the incident window (peak 01:20–03:50 UTC).
- Some sessions exhibited fragment interleaving (parts from two different responses merged out-of-order).
- Elevated token usage contributed to a billing delta (temporary credit issued — see Resolution).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: cumulus-dedicated-us-east (reserved capacity).
- Models used: redwood-8k-v1 primary, redwood-quant-4bit-v1 as fallback.
- Traffic routed through api-gateway cluster rgw-3 and routing control-plane region us-east-ctrl.

Steps to reproduce (observed in customer traffic):
1) Start a multi-turn streaming chat against their pinned model (redwood-8k-v1).
2) During a reservoir spike (>180 rps), routing control-plane health-checks flagged a subset of model hosts as degraded and initiated fallback to redwood-quant-4bit-v1.
3) Requests for long-context sessions got partially served by host A (old KV state) then re-routed mid-stream to host B (different KV prefix), producing interleaved chunks and duplicate partial completions.

Observed behavior / logs:
- api-gateway logs show rapid route flips for a subset of session IDs: route-change events within single request lifetime. (logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/us-east/rgw-3/2026-03-10/stream-flip-*.gz)
- Serving runtime traces show mismatched KV-cache-version headers (kv-v: 17 vs kv-v: 18) across stream fragments for the same session id.
- Control plane health-checks returned transient 503s to router with increased flapping between 01:18–01:36 UTC.
- Linked incident on status page INC-20260310-03 (routing failover automation triggered).

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Support enabled sticky routing for affected customer (sticky until session end) at 01:40 UTC to prevent mid-stream handoff.
- Disabled cross-variant automatic fallback for sessions with active KV cache > 1k tokens.
- Opened emergency SRE rotation and paused a pending routing rollout.

Customer impact and communication:
- Customer sent urgent escalation via account channel at 01:30 UTC. Support acknowledged at 01:34 UTC and provided mitigation timeline.
- Customer-facing SLO degradation: brief stream corruption and billing exposure. Credits offered and accepted (details in Resolution).

Next actions (follow-up):
- Short-term: add KV-cache-version propagation to routing handshake to avoid cross-variant mismatches.
- Medium-term: add atomic route handoff that drains active KV namespaces before switching host for sticky sessions.
- Postmortem: full RCA and retro, update runbook for routing rollout safety checks.

investigation_notes: 01:18–01:36 UTC: routing control-plane health-checks reported transient increased latency for backend host group A; automation triggered fallback to quant variant for some requests.
Trace evidence: stream fragments for session s-8a7f2 show kv-v header 17 then 18 within ~2s window; fragments merged by client produced interleaving.

Hypothesis: control-plane triggered fallback mid-request while downstream runtime had active KV state tied to original host; fallback host served partial completion without cache priming, so fragments had different context.
Reproduction attempt in staging: simulated host flapping with synthetic traffic produced deterministic interleaving when route-change occurred before 'kv-cache primed' event completed on new host.
Telemetry: affected request IDs clustered to a subset of router instances (rgw-3b/rgw-3c) behind a recent BGP overlay change that increased control-plane latency under burst load.
resolution:
Root cause: routing control-plane health-check flapping combined with non-atomic route handoffs allowed mid-request re-routing to hosts with different KV cache versions, causing fragment interleaving and duplicate partial outputs.

Fixes applied:
- Immediate: enabled per-session sticky routing and disabled cross-variant fallback for long-context sessions during the incident window.
- Patch: added kv-cache-version propagation in routing metadata and a 500ms drain/priming window before finalizing route switch (PR merged).
- Operational: paused the in-progress routing rollout linked to the BGP overlay change; added canary safety checks to prevent mid-request flips.
- Customer remediation: issued a partial billing credit for the affected window and scheduled a technical deep-dive; customer accepted credit on 2026-03-12.

Follow-ups assigned:
- ENG: implement atomic route handoff and KV version gating (owner: Marco Ruiz, ETA: 2026-03-25).
- SRE: add routing health-check smoothing and per-router telemetry alerting (owner: Anya Patel, ETA: 2026-03-18).
- Support: coordinate postmortem and customer-facing RCA document (owner: Sofia Morales, ETA: 2026-03-17).
